title: Platform systems & services playbook: runbooks, dashboards, roadmap
author: Marina Kovalenko
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates core platform engineering guidance for systems & services owned by Eng / Platform: operational runbooks, dashboards & alerts, how-tos for common tasks, retrospectives practices, and a concise roadmap. It is intended for oncall engineers, platform owners, and SRE partners. Read start-to-finish for context; follow the linked runbooks for step-by-step procedures.

1) Scope and ownership

- Scope: control plane services (route-manager, policy-gateway, model-router), observability pipeline (metrics-collector, log-ingest, tracing), and platform orchestration (autoscaler, scheduler).
- Primary owners: Platform Systems team. Secondary owners: Serving Runtime, Infra, Eng SRE.

Contact matrix (role -> pager):
| Component | Primary owner | Pager (rotation) | Slack channel |
|---|---|---:|---|
| route-manager | Platform Systems | oncall-platform | #platform-route-manager |
| metrics-collector | Eng SRE | oncall-sre | #observability |
| autoscaler | Platform Systems | oncall-platform | #autoscaler |

2) Dashboards & alerting standards

Purpose: dashboards provide quick incident triage and postmortem data; alerts should be actionable, with clear ownership and runbook links.

Dashboard naming and layout
- Prefix: platform.{component}.{view} (e.g., platform.route-manager.overview).
- Top row: availability and SLO panels (p99 latency, error rate, request rate).
- Middle: resource utilization (GPU/CPU/memory), queue/backlog metrics.
- Bottom: downstream & upstream health (e.g., model-store latency).

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- High-severity (P0): service_unavailable (HTTP 5xx > 5% sustained for 3m), kafka_consumer_lag > 10k for 5m.
- Medium-severity (P1): p99_latency > 2s for 10m, error_rate > 1% for 10m.
- Low-severity (P2): disk_usage > 85% on critical nodes, SLO burn rate > 2x for 1h.

Alert structure (template):
- Title: [component] short-description (severity)
- Symptoms: short bullet list of observed metrics.
- Impact: API endpoints, customers, internal dashboards affected.
- Owner: primary oncall and secondary.
- Runbook: link to section or page with steps.
- Mitigation knobs: e.g., scale-up autoscaler, route to degraded model, flush caches.

3) Key runbooks (summaries + canonical links)

A. Service-unavailable (5xx spike)
- Symptoms: 5xx > 5% sustained for 3m, elevated error logs with repeated stacktrace.
- Triage steps (ordered):
  1. Confirm alert and link to dashboard.
 2. Check recent deploys: `git log --max-count=5 --pretty=oneline` + CI deploy window.
  3. Verify downstream dependencies (model-store, auth) and circuit-breakers.
  4. If cause unknown and service degraded, trigger emergency rollback to last stable revision.
  5. If resource exhaustion, scale the fleet (see Autoscaler quick commands below).
  6. Notify stakeholders (post to #incident and pager).
- Recovery verification: traffic returning to baseline, error rate < 0.5% for 15m.

B. High request latency (p99 > threshold)
- Triage steps:
  1. Identify whether latency is CPU-bound, GPU-queue bound, or network. Use `platform.telemetry.latency_breakdown` panel.
  2. Check KV cache hit rate; if low, warm caches for hot prefixes.
  3. If GPU queue length > threshold, scale up or increase batch size if safe.
  4. If caused by a model change, roll forward or back to a stable model variant.

C. Observability pipeline outage (metrics/logs/traces missing)
- Triage steps:
  1. Confirm ingestion metrics: `ingest.events_per_minute` and `ingest.errors`.
  2. If errors indicate auth failures, verify KMS tokens and service account keys.
  3. If message broker (Kafka) down, failover to standby cluster per Kafka runbook.
  4. Restore backlog processing and validate historical fill.

Autoscaler quick commands (kubectl & CLI examples)
- Scale to N replicas: `./platformctl scale --component autoscaler --replicas 6 --env prod`
- Force an immediate scale down mitigation: `./platformctl drain --component route-manager --mode maintenance`

4) How-tos (common tasks)

A. Add a new dashboard panel
1. Open Grafana: /grafana/d/platform-mix
2. Create panel using metric: `platform.<component>.<metric>`
3. Set alert rule if panel is critical; include runbook link.
4. Save with versioned name: platform.{component}.{metric}.v{minor}

B. Create an alert policy
1. Draft condition in Alertmanager rules file.
2. Include `severity` and `pager` labels.
3. Add human-readable `summary` and `description` including runbook link.
4. Submit PR to infra-alerts repo and request review from Eng SRE.

C. Onboard a new service to platform systems
- Requirements checklist (table):
| Requirement | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Health endpoints | service owner | /healthz returns OK, /metrics exposed |
| SLO definition | service owner | SLOs declared in service-meta config |
| Dashboard | platform team | Overview & SLO panels created |
| Runbook | service owner | Runbook page with triage steps and rollback plan |

5) Retrospectives & blameless postmortems

- When to run: incidents with customer impact or P0/P1 events.
- Template: summary, timeline, root cause analysis, detection & mitigation, action items with owners and due dates.
- Follow-up: add preventive work to platform roadmap; track implementation in weekly platform sync.

6) Roadmap highlights (next 12 months)

- Q2-Q3 2025: Autoscaler v2 (predictive scaling using traffic patterns), improved cold-start mitigation for private deployments.
- Q4 2025: Observability pipeline resiliency (hot-path in-memory buffer + failover ingestion), unified service metadata catalog.
- Q1 2026: Self-serve dashboard-authoring experience for service owners; RBAC for panels.

7) Post-incident checklist and KPIs to track

- Postmortem posted within 72 hours.
- Action items assigned and scheduled in backlog (owner + due date).
- KPIs: Mean Time To Detect (MTTD), Mean Time To Recover (MTTR), SLO breach frequency, pager fatigue (alerts per oncall per week).

8) Team wiki & knowledge hygiene

- Maintain a one-line summary and owner on every page. Keep runbooks current after every significant change.
- Archive pages older than 2 years unless they have a documented owner.
- Weekly platform office hours: triage new dashboard requests and review open runbook PRs.

Appendix A — Troubleshooting checklist (copyable)
1) Confirm alert and gather dashboards URL.
2) Identify recent deploys and config changes (last 30 minutes).
3) Check resource utilization and queue lengths.
4) Review recent error logs and stack traces.
5) If unclear, escalate to senior oncall and open an incident in PagerDuty.

Appendix B — Useful links
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal.platform/
- Alertmanager: https://alertmanager.internal.platform/
- Platform CLI docs: internal://platformctl/docs
- Incident template: internal://postmortem/template

Ownership & maintenance
- Owner: Platform Systems (doc owner: Marina Kovalenko).
- Review cadence: quarterly.
- Last reviewed: 2025-02-18.

If you have a suggestion or find a missing runbook step, open a PR against confluence content repo or post to #platform-docs.
